name: request-access-dialog
title: Request access dialog
description: For someone who lands on something they cannot open: ask the owner for access with an optional note, then see that it was sent and what happens next.
docs: Pass resourceName, owner ({ name, email, image }), levels ({ id, label, description }; with a single level the choice is left out), onRequest({ level, message }) and, when you know it, signedInAs, which says as whom the person is asking and where the answer will go. onRequest may return a promise: the fields lock, the button shows progress and the dialog will not close; on success the form becomes 'Request sent to Maya Okafor' with what happens next and focus on Close when the focus was in the panel (a panel that nobody pressed by hand never takes focus or scrolls the page), and on a rejection the form stays with the note still in it and the Error's message above the buttons. pendingSince (a Date, an ISO string or a timestamp) recognises a repeat request: a notice reads 'Already requested 2 hours ago' and the button offers Send again. Pass now to get those words in server HTML, otherwise they appear once the browser's clock is read; locale and timeZone shape the words and the dates. maxLength limits the note (default 280, counted by the textarea counter), showOwnerEmail adds the owner's address (off by default: it is theirs to share), and Ctrl or Command with Enter sends from the note. trigger is the element that opens the dialog, open, defaultOpen and onOpenChange control it, RequestAccessPanel is the inside on its own (standalone), and labels translates every word.
